limitations: Agreement of the 33 non-canonical associative-looking specs with their formulas is verified on [0,64)^2 only.
novelty_basis: Each formula is classical or elementary - nim-sum and nim-product (Conway, On Numbers and Games, 1976); a + b and min(a, b) are the Grundy functions of 'reduce either or both heaps' and 'reduce both heaps' (rank functions of product posets). The census of a 512-member family and the resulting classification were not found (one web search, OEIS); small.
proof_check: written proof for the 11 canonical formulas (proofs/paper/C07.md Theorem 1(a), induction using Conway's mex lemmas); computer-assisted for non-associativity (explicit violating triples in [0,64)^3 for 468 specs, exact tables cross-checked against a plain implementation); awaiting independent skeptic review
statement:
In the family of 512 mex operations (options f(a',b) [L], f(a,b') [R] and XOR combinations of f(a',b),
f(a,b'), f(a',b') [D]), the canonical specs empty, L, R, D[x], D[y], D[z], L+R, D[x^y^z], L+R+D[z],
D[x]+D[y], D[x]+D[y]+D[z] define for all a, b the operations 0, a, b, a[b>0], b[a>0], min(a,b), a XOR b,
a (x) b (nim-product), a + b, ((a-1) XOR (b-1)) + 1 and a + b - 1 (the last two with 0 absorbing), all
associative; 468 of the 512 specs are not associative; the remaining 33 specs agree with one of the 11
operations on [0,64)^2.
title: The associative mex operations are 0, projections, min, +, XOR, nim-product and four relatives
